arxiv-2012-14344.title: Spectrum of periodic chain graphs with time-reversal non-invariant vertex coupling
arxiv-2012-14344.creator: Marzieh Baradaran, Pavel Exner, Miloš Tater
arxiv-2012-14344.description: Abstract We investigate spectral properties of quantum graphs in the form of a periodic chain of rings with a connecting link between each adjacent pair, assuming that wave functions at the vertices are matched through conditions manifestly non-invariant with respect to time reversal.

arxiv-2102-04255.title: AI Development for the Public Interest: From Abstraction Traps to Sociotechnical Risks Authors arranged alphabetically to indicate equal contribution.
arxiv-2102-04255.creator: McKane Andrus, Sarah Dean, Thomas Krendl Gilbert, Nathan Lambert, Tom Zick, McKane Andrus 1 , Sarah Dean 2 , Thomas Krendl Gilbert 3 , Nathan Lambert 2 and Tom Zick 4
arxiv-2102-04255.description: Abstract Despite interest in communicating ethical problems and social contexts within the undergraduate curriculum to advance Public Interest Technology (PIT) goals, interventions at the graduate level remain largely unexplored. This may be due to the conflicting ways through which distinct Artificial Intelligence (AI) research tracks conceive of their interface with social contexts.

arxiv-2204-01558.title: Con 2 DA: Simplifying Semi-supervised Domain Adaptation by Learning Consistent and Contrastive Feature Representations
arxiv-2204-01558.creator: Manuel Pérez-Carrasco, Pavlos Protopapas, Guillermo Cabrera-Vives
arxiv-2204-01558.description: Abstract In this work, we present Con 2 DA, a simple framework that extends recent advances in semi-supervised learning to the semi-supervised domain adaptation (SSDA) problem. Our framework generates pairs of associated samples by performing stochastic data transformations to a given input. Associated data pairs are mapped to a feature representation space using a feature extractor.

arxiv-2303-08726.title: The Number of Edges in Maximal 2-planar Graphs Thanks: Both the authors are supported by the Swiss National Science Foundation within the collaborative DACH project Arrangements and Drawings as SNSF Project 200021E-171681. This work (without appendix) is available at the 39th International Symposium
arxiv-2303-08726.creator: Michael Hoffmann, Meghana M. Reddy
arxiv-2303-08726.description: Abstract A graph is 2 2 -planar if it has local crossing number two, that is, it can be drawn in the plane such that every edge has at most two crossings. A graph is maximal 2 2 -planar if no edge can be added such that the resulting graph remains 2 2 -planar.

arxiv-2309-05789.title: Entropy current and entropy production in relativistic spin hydrodynamics
arxiv-2309-05789.creator: Francesco Becattini, Asaad Daher, Xin-Li Sheng
arxiv-2309-05789.description: Abstract We use a first-principle quantum-statistical method to derive the expression of the entropy production rate in relativistic spin hydrodynamics. We show that the entropy current is not uniquely defined and can be changed by means of entropy-gauge transformations, much the same way as the stress-energy tensor and the spin tensor can be changed with pseudo-gauge transformations.

arxiv-2404-12835.title: Distinguishing radiation mechanisms and particle populations in blazar jets through long-term multi-band monitoring with RINGO3 and Fermi
arxiv-2404-12835.creator: Callum McCall, Helen Jermak, Iain A. Steele, Iván Agudo, Ulisses Barres de Almeida, Talvikki Hovatta, Gavin P. Lamb, Elina Lindfors, Carole Mundell
arxiv-2404-12835.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Callum McCall, Helen Jermak, Iain A. Steele, Iván Agudo, Ulisses Barres de Almeida, Talvikki Hovatta, Gavin P. Lamb, Elina Lindfors, Carole Mundell. We present the results of seven years of multicolour photometric monitoring of a sample of 31 γ \gamma -ray bright blazars using the RINGO3 polarimeter on the Liverpool Telescope from 2013–2020.

arxiv-2412-06725.title: Harmonic Mean Density Fusion in Distributed Tracking: Performance and Comparison
arxiv-2412-06725.creator: Nikhil Sharma, Ratnasingham Tharmarasa, Thiagalingam Kirubarajan
arxiv-2412-06725.description: Abstract A distributed sensor fusion architecture is preferred in a real target-tracking scenario as compared to a centralized scheme since it provides many practical advantages in terms of computation load, communication bandwidth, fault-tolerance, and scalability. In multi-sensor target-tracking literature, such systems are better known by the pseudonym—track fusion, since processed tracks are fused instead of raw measurements.

arxiv-2503-03909.title: lrAA: Low-Rank Anderson Acceleration Thanks: Submitted to the editors August 24, 2026
arxiv-2503-03909.creator: Daniel Appelö, Yingda Cheng
arxiv-2503-03909.description: Abstract This paper proposes a new framework for computing low-rank solutions to nonlinear matrix equations arising from spatial discretization of nonlinear partial differential equations: low-rank Anderson acceleration (lrAA). lrAA is an adaptation of Anderson acceleration (AA), a well-known approach for solving nonlinear fixed point problems, to the low-rank format.

arxiv-2503-14358.title: RFMI: Estimating Mutual Information on Rectified Flow for Text-to-Image Alignment
arxiv-2503-14358.creator: Chao Wang, Giulio Franzese, Alessandro Finamore, Pietro Michiardi, EURECOM , Huawei Technologies SASU, France \textrm{EURECOM},\textrm{Huawei Technologies SASU, France}
arxiv-2503-14358.description: Abstract Rectified Flow (RF) models trained with a Flow matching framework have achieved state-of-the-art performance on Text-to-Image (T2I) conditional generation. Yet, multiple benchmarks show that synthetic images can still suffer from poor alignment with the prompt, i.e., images show wrong attribute binding, subject positioning, numeracy, etc.

arxiv-2505-06661.title: Centralized Trust in Decentralized Systems: Unveiling Hidden Contradictions in Blockchain and Cryptocurrency
arxiv-2505-06661.creator: Faisal Haque Bappy, EunJeong Cheon, Tariqul Islam
arxiv-2505-06661.description: Abstract . Blockchain technology promises to democratize finance and promote social equity through decentralization, but questions remain about whether current implementations advance or hinder these goals. Through a mixed-methods study combining semi-structured interviews with 13 diverse blockchain stakeholders and analysis of over 3,000 cryptocurrency discussions on Reddit, we examine how trust manifests in cryptocurrency ecosystems despite their decentralized architecture.

arxiv-2510-13870.title: Unlocking the Potential of Diffusion Language Models through Template Infilling
arxiv-2510-13870.creator: Junhoo Lee, Seungyeon Kim, Nojun Kwak
arxiv-2510-13870.description: Abstract Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to Autoregressive Language Models, yet their inference strategies remain limited to prefix-based prompting inherited from the autoregressive paradigm. In this paper, we propose Template Infilling (TI), a tailored conditioning methodology for DLMs’ generation process.

arxiv-2601-00255.title: Hydrodynamic flows induced by localized torques (rotlets) in wedge-shaped geometries
arxiv-2601-00255.creator: Abdallah Daddi-Moussa-Ider, Jakob Mihatsch, Michael J. Mitchell, Elsen Tjhung, Andreas M. Menzel
arxiv-2601-00255.description: Abstract Wedge-shaped geometries in low-Reynolds-number flows are of increasing importance, for instance, in the design of microfluidic devices. The corresponding Green’s functions describing the induced flow in response to a locally applied force were derived some time ago. To achieve a complete characterization of particle motion at low Reynolds numbers, we derive the flow response to locally applied torques.

Our objective was to investigate the immunological effects of prolonged sleep restrictio

pmc-10514085.title: The NCOR-HDAC3 co-repressive complex modulates the leukemogenic potential of the transcription factor ERG
pmc-10514085.creator: Eitan Kugler, Shreyas Madiwale, Darren Yong, Julie A. I. Thoms, Yehudit Birger, David B. Sykes, Johannes Schmoellerl, Aneta Drakul, Valdemar Priebe, Muhammad Yassin, Nasma Aqaqe, Avigail Rein, Hila Fishman, Ifat Geron, Chun-Wei Chen, Brian Raught, Qiao Liu, Heather Ogana, Elisabeth Liedke, Jean-Pier
pmc-10514085.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The ERG (ETS-related gene) transcription factor is linked to various types of cancer, including leukemia. However, the specific ERG domains and co-factors contributing to leukemogenesis are poorly understood. Drug targeting a transcription factor such as ERG is challenging. Our study reveals the critical role of a conserved amino acid, proline, at position 199, located at the 3’ end of the PNT (pointed) domain, in ERG’s ability to induce leukemia.

pmc-10614358.title: Bacterial genome-wide association study substantiates papGII of Escherichia coli as a major risk factor for urosepsis
pmc-10614358.creator: Aline Cuénod, Jessica Agnetti, Helena M B Seth-Smith, Tim Roloff, Denise Wälchli, Dimitri Shcherbakov, Rashid Akbergenov, Sarah Tschudin-Sutter, Stefano Bassetti, Martin Siegemund, Christian H Nickel, Jacob Moran-Gilad, Timothy G Keys, Valentin Pflüger, Nicholas R Thomson, Adrian Egli
pmc-10614358.description: BackgroundUrinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common bacterial infections worldwide, often caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli. Multiple bacterial virulence factors or patient characteristics have been linked separately to progressive, more invasive infections. In this study, we aim to identify pathogen- and patient-specific factors that drive the progression to urosepsis by jointly analysing bacterial and host characteristics.

pmc-11375708.title: Controlling Mechanical Properties of Medical-Grade Scaffolds through Electrospinning Parameter Selection
pmc-11375708.creator: Clayton
pmc-11375708.description: Electrospinning (ES) is a versatile process mode for creating fibrous materials with various structures that have broad applications ranging from regenerative medicine to tissue engineering and surgical mesh implants. The recent commercialization of this technology for implant use has driven the use of resorbable electrospun products.

pmc-11404217.title: Comparison of two implementation strategies for anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention in amateur girls’ youth soccer: a prospective cohort study
pmc-11404217.creator: William Suits, Meg Darmofal, Olivia Roe, Tzu-Chieh Liao
pmc-11404217.description: ObjectivesTo compare two implementation strategies, an educational handout and a knowledge-to-action (KTA) intervention, for promoting anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury prevention programme (ACL-IPP) implementation in amateur youth girls’ soccer. The primary outcomes assessed include frequency of ACL-IPP implementation and ACL injury risk.MethodsThis was a prospective cohort study, which followed 671 amateur female soccer players (15.72±1.

pmc-11625724.title: Summary of the best evidence for risk stratification of exercise rehabilitation in patients with a cardiac implantable electronic device
pmc-11625724.creator: Ruiqing Di, Zheng Huang, Huifang Huang, Siyu Li, Xing Gao, Jingshuang Bai
pmc-11625724.description: BackgroundHierarchical management of sports risk is highly critical to ensure the safety of sports rehabilitation. Early identification, timely prevention and control of sports-related risk factors, and enhanced supervision and guidance can provide a basis for the formulation of sports programmes and the setting of sports monitoring levels.

pmc-11713995.title: Diffusion‐Weighted MRI Brain Connectivity Assessment of Healthy Aging Trajectories in Marmosets
pmc-11713995.creator: Diego Szczupak, Rebecca Bhik‐Ghanie, Bei Zhang, Daniel Papoti, Vinicius Campos, Lauren R Dubberley, T Kevin Hitchens, Fang‐Cheng Yeh, Lauren K Hayrynen Schaeffer, Gregory W Carter, Stacey J Sukoff Rizzo, David J Schaeffer, Afonso C Silva
pmc-11713995.description: BackgroundThe common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) is an important animal model in neuroscience and neurological diseases (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease ‐ AD), as they present primate‐specific evolutionary features such as an expanded frontal cortex. We established a new consortium with funding support from the National Institute on Aging to generate, characterize, and validate MArmosets as Research MOdels of AD (MARMO‐AD).

pmc-12465053.title: Study on the effect of HMGB1 on immune cells isolated from SLE mice
pmc-12465053.creator: Xin Qin, Jinglin Gao, Xiuhua Liu, Jie Chen, Xinghui Song
pmc-12465053.description: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex autoimmune disease, and its pathogenesis is related to the balance and dysfunction of dendritic cells (DCs). The therapy targeting dendritic cells has become an important means to treat SLE and autoimmune diseases. Besides, HMGB1 is highly expressed in the serum of patients with SLE.

pmc-12593594.title: Dynamic changes of volatile compounds during coffee-grounds beer fermentation with different yeast strains: An integrated HS-SPME-GC/MS, electronic tongue and electronic nose analysis
pmc-12593594.creator: Jingan Yang, Jinyu Zhao, Jiashun Jiang, Dapeng Lu, Ye Lv, Lijing Liu, Hong Li
pmc-12593594.description: As a major coffee processing byproduct, spent coffee grounds (SCG) contain abundant bioactive compounds despite being typically discarded. This study analyzed flavor changes in coffee-grounds beer fermented with four yeast strains (Lalvin R2™ (R),Lalvin EC1118™ (E)，Lalvin ICVD254R(D)，Uvaferm43R(U)) through an integrated multi-omics approach.

pmc-12615265.title: Cell tracking with accurate error prediction
pmc-12615265.creator: Max A Betjes, Rutger N U Kok, Sander J Tans, Jeroen S van Zon
pmc-12615265.description: Cell tracking is an indispensable tool for studying development by time-lapse imaging. However, existing cell trackers cannot assign confidence to predicted tracks, which prohibits fully automated analysis without manual curation. We present a fundamental advance: an algorithm that combines neural networks with statistical physics to determine cell tracks with error probabilities for each step in the track.

pmc-13043706.title: Sustainable methylene blue dye removal via bio-derived micro/micron-sized porous particles Zygophyllum coccineum and Calotropis procera: A machine learning-assisted study
pmc-13043706.creator: Hala Fakry, Eslam Salama, Ayat Taha, Mona Ossman, Giuliano Bonanomi, Ahmed M. Abd-ElGawad, Yasser A. El-Amier
pmc-13043706.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The discharge of synthetic dyes into aquatic ecosystems poses a critical threat to environmental and human health, necessitating urgent, cost-effective, and sustainable remediation strategies. This study addresses a practical yet underexplored question in biosorption research: Is the additional energy and processing cost of converting plant-based materials from micro- to Micron-sized porous particles scale justified by a significantly higher dye removal performance?

pmc-13233134.title: Response to: The Long Game in Ulcerative Colitis: Mirikizumab’s Four-Year Outcomes
pmc-13233134.creator: David B Clemow
pmc-13233134.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). It is agreed that mirikizumab may “offer patients durable efficacy and long-term safety” with “stable maintenance dosing.”1

In relation to discussing missing data imputation methods, it is mentioned from the paper that 13% (40 of 316 total patients) of discontinuations in the long-term extension (4 years of continuous treatment) were due to patients switching to a commercially available drug. Please note that this equates to 30% (40/132) of discontinuations.

pmc-13528742.title: Posttraumatic stress in newly diagnosed epilepsy: associations with early maladaptive schemas, anxiety, and quality of life in a 6-month prospective study
pmc-13528742.creator: Mehmet ÖZTÜRK, Pınar ÖZTÜRK, Fügen SÖNMEZ ÇETİNKAYA, İlker ÖZDEMİR
pmc-13528742.description: Background/aimEpilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that significantly affects psychosocial functioning, self-perception, and quality of life. Emerging evidence suggests that posttraumatic stress (PTS) symptoms may be more prevalent in individuals with epilepsy than previously recognized, particularly following seizure-related experiences perceived as traumatic.

pmc-13541642.title: Current status and prospects in diagnosis of major opportunistic fungal infections among HIV-positive population in south provinces of China and neighboring countries that are suffering high prevalence of AIDS
pmc-13541642.creator: Guanmei Lu, Jing Dan, Xuelian Yang, Lei Tan, Junjun Jiang
pmc-13541642.description: Highlights:•Limitations of conventional fungal diagnostics (culture/microscopy) are summarized, while novel molecular tools enable rapid pathogen identification.•Emerging platforms including ddPCR, SERS and nanopore sequencing are assessed for use in resource-limited endemic regions.•AI and machine learning improve early fungal diagnosis and facilitate individualized patient treatment strategies.•Regional cooperation and capacity construction help upgrade diagnostic infrastructure against cross-border fungal threats.
